stem:
**P**, **Q** and **R** all have the molecular formula $\text{C}_3\text{H}_6\text{O}$. They are all structural isomers of each other.

**P** and **Q** each contain an oxygen atom bonded directly to a carbon atom that is $\text{sp}^2$ hybridised. **R** contains an oxygen atom bonded directly to a carbon atom that is $\text{sp}^3$ hybridised.

parts.label: (a)(i)
parts.text: Explain the meaning of the term *structural isomers*.

parts.label: (a)(ii)
parts.text: Explain how $\text{sp}^2$ and $\text{sp}^3$ hybridisation can occur in carbon atoms.

parts.label: (a)(iii)
parts.text: State the bond angles normally associated with each type of hybridisation in carbon atoms.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
**R** contains two different functional groups, one of which is an alkene group.

**R** reacts with cold, dilute, acidified manganate(VII) ions to form propane-1,2,3-triol.

{{figure:pdf_visual_01.png}}

propane-1,2,3-triol

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text: State the type of reaction and what you would observe when **R** reacts with bromine water.

parts.label: (b)(iii)
parts.text: Draw the structure of the product formed when **R** reacts with bromine water.

parts.label: (b)(iv)
parts.text: Identify the gaseous product formed when **R** reacts with hot, concentrated, acidified manganate(VII) ions.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text: **P** and **Q** ($\text{C}_3\text{H}_6\text{O}$) both form an orange precipitate when reacted with 2,4-DNPH. Only **Q** produces a yellow precipitate when reacted with alkaline aqueous iodine.

parts.label: (c)(ii)
parts.text: Identify the yellow precipitate formed by the reaction of **Q** with alkaline aqueous iodine.

parts.label: (d)
parts.text:
**P** and **Q** each react with hydrogen cyanide to form a single product.

The product formed from **P** exists as a pair of optical isomers.

The product formed from **Q** does not exhibit optical isomerism.

parts.label: (d)(i)
parts.text: Explain the meaning of the term *optical isomers*.

parts.label: (d)(ii)
parts.text:
Ethanal, $\text{CH}_3\text{CHO}$, also reacts with hydrogen cyanide. The product of this reaction is $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)CN}$.

Draw the mechanism of this reaction.

Include all necessary charges, dipoles, lone pairs and curly arrows.
